Equality delete files (defined for #360) should have a reader and writer for engines to use when encoding deletes.
The writer should accept either a row of values to be written to the file, or a row from which the values are extracted.
title: Add reader and writer implementations for equality delete files
Add reader and writer implementations for position-based delete files

body:
Position-based delete files encode row deletes as a file and ordinal row position within that file. To write position-based delete files for Avro, Iceberg should produce the file and position for a given row as metadata columns.
The file metadata column is a constant and can reuse the id-to-constant map that sets identity-partition values.
The position metadata column will need to keep a counter from the first row in the file (starting at 0). When reading an Avro split that doesn't start at offset 0, the Avro reader will need to scan through Avro blocks from the start of the file. Each Avro block contains a long count of objects in the block and a long size of the compressed block in bytes. Reconstructing the position of a row will require reading each block header to count the bytes in blocks before the start of a split.
title: Add _file and _pos metadata columns to Avro readers

body:
Position-based delete files encode row deletes as a file and ordinal row position within that file. To write position-based delete files for Parquet, Iceberg should produce the file and position for a given row as metadata columns.
The file metadata column is a constant and can reuse the id-to-constant map that sets identity-partition values.
The position metadata column will require tracking the starting position of the first row in each row group using footer metadata, and using a counter within each row group to produce the final position value.
title: Add _file and _pos metadata columns to Parquet readers

body:
Position-based delete files encode row deletes as a file and ordinal row position within that file. To write position-based delete files for ORC, Iceberg should produce the file and position for a given row as metadata columns.
The file metadata column is a constant and can reuse the id-to-constant map that sets identity-partition values.
The position metadata column will require tracking the starting position of the first row in each stripe using footer metadata, and using a counter within each stripe to produce the final position value.
title: Add _file and _pos metadata columns to ORC readers

body: Position-based delete files will be applied using a row filter. The filter should bind to a record schema using accessors, like expression evaluators. Because position-based delete files are required to be sorted, the filter should use a merge strategy instead of loading deletes for a file into memory.
title: Add a row filter implementation for position-based deletes

body:
Equality deletes will be applied in row-based reads using a row filter. The filter should bind to the projected record schema using accessors, like expression evaluators. Because the order in an equality delete file is not guaranteed to match the order of incoming rows, the most generic filter should build a hash set of rows from equality delete files and filter out data file rows that produce a "key" row in the set.
Note that when Iceberg tracks sort order for delete and data files, a merge strategy can be used in place of the set-based filter if the delete and data file sort order matches. This optimization is tracked by #1024.
title: Add a row filter implementation for equality deletes

body: When Iceberg tracks the sort order of data and delete files, a merge-based strategy can be used to filter rows instead of a set-based strategy (#1023) when the order of a delete file matches the order of a data file.
title: Add a merge-based row filter for equality deletes

body: In format v2, partition fields are required to have unique field IDs to support partition spec evolution. This should be documented in the spec, along with notes about handling tables without partition field IDs.
title: Spec: Document field-id requirements for partition specs

body: Tables with slowly changing data may have many small delete files, with only a small portion of the data affected. In that case, it may not be worth rewriting data files to remove rows. Iceberg should provide an action to compact delete files to minimize delete files in a task that need to be read and to keep the number of files in memory during job planning lower.
title: Add an action to compact delete files

body: Tables will eventually need to apply deletes to data files and remove deleted rows. Iceberg should provide an action to do this.
title: Add an action to rewrite data files and remove deleted rows

body: Replacing an entire table is a supported action that replaces the schema of a table along with all of the data. The use case is reporting tables, where the data completely changes from day to day and it makes little sense to maintain the schema using DDL when the report is generated using a CTAS or RTAS query. For these tables, each snapshot may have its own schema and reading an older snapshot should use that snapshot's schema.
title: Spec: Add schema IDs, schema list, and associate each Snapshot with a schema

We use spark options to send hadoop configurations (specifically mentioned below), to read/write to Iceberg table. These options have helped in reading/writing when we have multiple SparkSession (which shares hadoop configuration on Global spark Context), each belonging to a tenant, and each tenant can potentially have different creds (have different ACLs as well).
There is multi tenant configuration also available like dfs.adls.oauth2.client.id.{accountName}, which can be set on sparkContext, but we don't want to expose the creds from one session to other. Make sense? I think it will help in scenarios, when even multi tenant hadoop configuration aren't supported by underlying store.
NOTE: This is already supported here.
Working on a fix.

body:
As far as I know, currently, users can only work with iceberg on an existing hadoop / hdfs / hive / spark cluster or deploying a new one. It's not very friendly to starters, especially those who want to know more about iceberg but don't have an available environment to make iceberg work well. I believe there're many users like me in situations like:

users that cannot try iceberg because of limitations like (spark / hdfs / hive version).
users that work with other frameworks (like Flink), want to know more about iceberg.
users that want to demonstrate the capability of Iceberg to other potential users.

I'm proposing this because I'm exploring the data lake related frameworks right now and Hudi already has the Docker Demo and it helps me to demonstrate the demo to other members in the same team.
I believe this also will do a lot of help to starters in Iceberg, and I can work on this if committers think this's worth doing.
title: Add docker demo for iceberg starters
